title: Oxido-inflammatory and neurotoxic responses of Bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate-exposed Nauphoeta cinerea nymphs across developmental time points
content:
Abstract
Bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (BEHP) is known to cause detrimental effects in plants and animals when released into the environment. However, its toxicological effect on Nauphoeta cinerea nymphs has not been reported. Hence, this study investigated the oxido-inflammatory and neurotoxic effects of environmentally relevant concentrations of BEHP (0, 2.5, 5.0, and 10 μg/L) in N. cinerea on the head and midgut at different stages of nymphal development, particularly 7, 21, and 42 days’ exposure periods. The neurobehavioral assessment using the open field showed that BEHP resulted in a diminution in locomotory activity and an upsurge in anxiety-like behaviour as evidenced by the decrease in total distance traveled, maximum speed, total time mobile, body rotations, turn angle, and path efficiency, with an upsurge in total freezing time during the 7-, 21-, and 42-day periods. Notably, BEHP exposure time- and concentration-dependently diminished acetylcholinesterase activity in the head, and antioxidant status in N. cinerea nymphs by decreasing the activities of catalase, glutathione-S-transferase, superoxide dismutase, and glutathione peroxidase, with glutathione level in the head and midguts of N. cinerea nymphs. Exposure of N. cinerea nymphs to BEHP time- and concentration-dependently increased oxido-inflammatory parameters, including lipid peroxidation, hydrogen peroxide, and nitric oxide levels in the head and midguts. Furthermore, alkaline phosphatase and acid phosphatase activities in the midgut of N. cinerea nymphs exposed to BEHP decreased during the 7, 21-, and 42-day exposure periods. Overall, BEHP induces sublethal physiological and behavioural alterations in N. cinerea nymphs in a concentration- and time-dependent manner.
